skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer clearly stated the Committee and company are the clients, not the witness; counsel cannot give legal advice to the witness; this was given at the very start.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains the privilege belongs to the company, the company decides on waiver, and it may disclose the interview without the witness's consent or notice.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explains how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, tells the witness to flag speculation and to separate recollection from uncertainty, in a professional tone.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks if the witness understands and has questions; T4 has the witness restate who is represented and who controls privilege, checking understanding.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: Witness left at T151; at T152 the interviewer gave a confidentiality reminder, asked to keep documents and notes, and offered to continue. No other-witness or nothing-else question was possible.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Explained how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, and set ground rules on speculation and distinguishing recollection from reconstruction.
Reminded the witness to keep documents and notes and keep the matter confidential as he left.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Repeatedly opened topics with open invitations such as Tell me everything you remember (T16, T32, T44, T80) and let the witness walk through events.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moves from role and reporting lines (T8-T14) to open narrative (T16) and then to specifics on each transaction, a sensible general-to-specific order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear, but some are compound or legalistic, such as T30 and T136, and T150 asks the witness to explain a combination of facts.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Stayed neutral and polite under pressure, including when the witness bristled at T151; the interviewer kept control and closed courteously.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Changed course when answers were evasive, for example probing 'various considerations' at T50, the proxy aim at T52, and the Foundation return at T142-T150, though it did not chase the Chewco and Skilling leads.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Pressed for a best estimate after the witness said he was estimating returns, and asked clearly.

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Challenged hedges such as T57, T83, T125 and T143-T150, but left the Kopper own-account claim at T79 unchallenged.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Covers who, what, when and how for LJM1, the unwind, Chewco and Southampton Place, but leaves key who and how gaps on Chewco ownership and approvals.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: At T62 asked about notes or minutes, then showed the November 5, 1997 minutes at T70 after the witness's own recollection; the approach was reasonable.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Separated personal knowledge from hearsay at T56-T57 and T82-T83, and asked how the witness knew of timing at T96-T97, but did not do this for Kopper's role.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: Asked who in Causey's group reviewed the unwind (T40-T43) and got the names of Causey and his staff, but did not ask about Glisan or Kopper as witnesses.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: Raised minutes (T62-T70), approval sheets (T88-T101), investor reports (T117) and foundation statements (T147), though it did not request the approval sheets directly.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Asked how certain the witness was of the $4.5M figure (T144) and asked for a best estimate of returns (T118), but did not test the witness's certainty on Chewco or Skilling.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Followed up most key leads, but two key leads (T79 Kopper's own-account claim and T103 blank Skilling line) were never followed up, which caps the score at 2.

missed_chances.description: Skilling's approval line was left blank on the Raptor I approval sheet, a control failure that was never pursued.
missed_chances.question: Why was Skilling's approval line left blank on the Raptor I sheet, and who decided the deal could proceed without it?

tips: Ask: What economic interest did you, your family, or Kopper have in Chewco, and when did you first learn of it?
Ask: For each approval sheet, who signed and when, what did those reviewers see before signing, and why was Skilling's line blank on Raptor I?
